I'm not looking for top of the line ammo. I'm just looking at something to shoot and build my supply with. Does anyone have any horror stories about shoddy reloads?

Example 1 2 3

Edit: Looking spicifically for a Beretta 92FS. Also, what do you think about rifle vs pistol reloads?
What are your thoughts on buying reloaded bulk ammo?

I think you'd want to start with the assumption that the level of quality control would be lower than what you are used to.

This is OK if you are, for example, buying .38 special ammo to shoot in the .357 revolver - an unexpectedly stiff charge isn't likely to hurt anything. It's not OK if you are buying .40 ammo for a pocket pistol. The .40 is sensitive to things like bullet setback and small changes in powder levels, and small guns allow for smaller margins of error.

9mm? I wouldn't shoot that stuff in a collectable luger, or in a pocket gun, but a full-sized steel gun like a Beretta 92 can safely absorb a little more variety in its diet. It's a judgement call and you have to just do what seems best to you.
I was looking at it for a Beretta 92FS. What about rifle vs pistol reloads?

As with pistols, some rounds are more sensitive than others. Smaller, higher-pressure stuff is always going to be more demanding.

Heavy bolt action guns are pretty strong; semi autos, especially older ones, not so much. A bolt action will also give you some warning if the round is chambering with more difficulty that usual.

Kromulent's advice seems pretty sound to me. I've never had any significant problems with reloaded ammo, but ya just can't ever say it couldn't be problematic. Buying from reputable outlets is also probably a plus, too. I'm assuming, and only assuming, that they wouldn't be selling it if there any huge likelihood of liability to them. But ya never know. I think a good solid firearm is the best key ... and as already stated, I wouldn't be as confident in an older, or less sturdy arm.
